title: Powers of an element with smooth free localization are strictly standard
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a ring map of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $a\in A$ such that the localization $A_a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and the module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a stably free $A_a$-module, i.e. $\Omega_{A_a/R}\oplus A_a^{\oplus s}\cong A_a^{\oplus t}$ for some integers $s,t\ge0$ (for instance free of finite rank, $s=0$). Then there is an integer $e_0\ge1$ such that $a^e$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] for every $e\ge e_0$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard, line 719), part (e) [(2) => a^e strictly standard for e >= e_0], with (3) => (2) of part (a) for free Omega

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation P0 with Presentation.exists_presentation_fin. Apply Presentation.localized_conormal_equiv. Convert hstable from finitely supported coordinates to function coordinates. Associate the products and compose the conormal complement equivalence with the inverse of hstable to give (B tensor_A P0.Cotangent) plus B^t equiv B^(n0+s). This is the explicit linear equivalence eM in Lean.

Apply the stabilized localized conormal basis theorem to P0 and eM, obtaining P, c<=min(n,m), and the specified initial basis. Apply the localized conormal-basis Jacobian theorem to this same P and basis, obtaining localized relation membership and a localized matrix left inverse.

Apply IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff to each remaining relation to obtain a power of h=P.sigma(a) carrying it into K. Multiplying by further powers preserves ideal membership. The difference P.sigma(a^e)-h^e is in the kernel by evaluation. Its product with any relation lies in I^2, so the condition holds for the required chosen lift P.sigma(a^e). Take e1 as the finite supremum of these exponents.

The proved private helper common_denominator clears a common power of a from the finitely many entries of the localized left inverse L. Matrix.map_mul shows the error B0 D-a^u 1 vanishes locally. IsLocalization.Away.exists_of_eq kills every entry by a power; a finite supremum yields V. Scaling B0 by a^V gives B D=a^(V+u)1, as proved by private clear_matrix_left_inverse.

Apply scalar_left_inverse_maximal_minors to B D=a^e2 1. It supplies the actual Cauchy-Binet coefficients expressing a^(e2*c) as a sum of row minors. Matrix.det_transpose identifies these row minors with the ordered Jacobian minors in IsStrictlyStandardElement. For e>=e2*c multiply coefficients by a^(e-e2*c).

Set e0=max 1 (max e1 (e2*c)). The two previously proved bounds give both defining conditions for every e>=e0, using the same presentation and c. Unfold IsStrictlyStandardElement and provide the explicit multiplied Cauchy-Binet coefficients.

lean.statement:
theorem smooth_free_differentials_strictly_standard_power
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [FinitePresentation R A] (a : A)
    [Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away a)]
    (s t : ℕ)
    (hstable : Nonempty
      ((KaehlerDifferential R (Localization.Away a) × (Fin s →₀ Localization.Away a))
        ≃ₗ[Localization.Away a] (Fin t →₀ Localization.Away a))) :
    ∃ e₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ e₀ ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, e₀ ≤ e →
      IsStrictlyStandardElement (R := R) (a ^ e)
